a: No. It records what you do on the page: what you point at and click, what you draw, and what you say or type, with timestamps. That's what lets it name the exact element for each change. There is no video, so there's nothing to upload and nothing for an agent to watch.

q: Which coding agents does it work with?
a: Any agent that reads text: the brief is plain Markdown (and JSON). With the Claude Code plugin, the toolbar's Send to agent button delivers it to Claude Code directly, and /pointbrief:apply makes the changes and shows you the diff. Cursor can use the same MCP server, or you paste the brief.

q: Does it work with React, Vue, Svelte or plain HTML?
a: It works on any web page. In React (including React 19), Vue 3 and Svelte development builds, and with build plugins that annotate source files, each target also names its component and source file. In plain HTML you get the selector, text and styles, which is usually enough for an agent to find the code.

To your browser's speech recognition. Chrome on desktop can transcribe on the device once it has the language pack; otherwise browsers send audio to their own speech service (Google's for Chrome, Apple's for Safari). The toolbar tells you which applies before you start, and Type instead keeps everything on the page. Pointbrief itself has no server.

q: Can I use it on my production site?
a: It's built for your app in development. Add the script in development only (the docs show how for Vite, Next.js, Nuxt and SvelteKit). The bridge to Claude Code accepts briefs only from local pages such as localhost.
